conviction_note: First print as a public company for a 6-week-old AI data-center power IPO that has fallen from $18 to a $9.95 low (Nov 5) and bounced ~28% to ~$12.8 into the print; peers that reported after the IPO (Vertiv, Eaton, nVent) were strong and the $1.1B June backlog covers H2 consensus ~2.4x, but the Q3 bar is unsourced, gross margin was compressing, Microsoft flagged third-party capacity delays and the stock just ran into the print, so p_up sits at 53 on a large (14%) unsigned move; impact_sum (+0.6) and the scaled number (+0.84) agree in sign and size.
bar: Partly unsourced. FY2026 revenue consensus $901.7M (range $898.2-904.0M, S&P Global, 8 analysts) and FY26 EPS $0.50, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/accv/forecast/ (as of 2026-11-04). With H1 2026 revenue of $437.5M (S-1, https://pulse2.com/accelevation-files-for-ipo-with-1-1-billion-backlog-following-147-revenue-growth/amp/) that implies H2 ~$464M, i.e. Q3 roughly $225-235M. The only explicit Q3 figure found, $0.19B revenue / $0.09 EPS at https://www.nextearningsdate.com/accv.html (updated 2026-11-06), contradicts that implied split and has no named source. No company guide was published (no 8-K item 2.02 or guidance release since the IPO). Because Q3 cannot be sourced to a guide or to two agreeing estimate sources, every finding that depends on the bar is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 3.9M shares, reported as 3.3% of float, up 38.2%, days to cover 3.0 (StockTitan, https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/ACCV/, read 2026-11-12). That 3.3% is measured against all ~120M Class A shares, but the 2026-11-10 Schedule 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2141406/000162828026072893/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X01/primary_doc.xml) shows Olympus entities directly holding 87.2M of the Class A shares plus 105.0M Class B, controlling 85.4%. The tradable public float is therefore about 33M shares, and 3.9M short is roughly 12% of it. An earlier MarketBeat snapshot read 2.84M short with 1.1 days to cover (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-accelevation-nasdaq-accv-upgraded-at-barclays-2026-10-27/). IBKR borrow fee was 4.1% on 2026-10-25, down from 13.9% at listing, with about 850k shares available (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/accv/borrow-fee/). No option-implied move or skew was found: the baseline carries none and searches returned nothing. Price path: IPO $18 (2026-09-30), $13.05 on 2026-10-26, -17.1% on 2026-11-04, $9.95 close on 2026-11-05, $11.91 close on 2026-11-11 (+11.5%), $12.78 at 12:18 on 2026-11-12 (+7.3%). So the stock is about 29% below its IPO price but about 28% off its low in five sessions.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after ACCV's IPO all showed data-center power demand accelerating in the September quarter: Vertiv (10-28) Americas sales +66% organic, organic orders >100%, FY26 sales guide raised $650M; Eaton (11-03) Electrical Americas data-center sales +54%, rolling-12M orders +39%, backlog +33%; nVent (10-30) sales +44% and FY organic guide raised to 38-39%, but orders grew only low double digits and Q4 is guided down to 26-29% on supplier capacity. ACCV's sell-side models were built off the roadshow before any of these prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable history: this is ACCV's first print as a public company, and the sweep marked the baseline history untrustworthy. For the peers, Vertiv rose 16.5% on its 10-28 beat-and-raise (https://www.trefis.com/stock/vrt/articles/623340/what-is-behind-the-drop-in-vertiv-stock/2026-11-06), then gave it back in the 11-04/05 policy selloff.
findings.why_not_priced: ACCV's price has moved on the sector's political risk, not on its demand. It fell 17% on 11-04 and to $9.95 on 11-05 along with Vertiv (-13%, then -14%) after the midterms and the Texas governor-elect's moratorium pledge. If the peer demand read were priced, ACCV would not be at 25x a FY26 EPS that S&P's eight analysts set in late October, below every initiating target ($16-22). The five initiations of 10-26 predate Eaton's 11-03 print.
findings.independence: Three separate companies and documents. Eaton: https://finviz.com/news/414001/eaton-reports-record-third-quarter-2026-results-with-strong-organic-growth-accelerating-record-orders-and-backlog-raises-organic-growth-guidance (2026-11-03). nVent: https://finviz.com/news/412747/nvent-beats-and-raises-again-but-lagging-orders-and-a-q4-slowdown-keep-the-bulls-on-the-defensive (2026-10-30). All three are proxies (peers), not ACCV's own number.

findings.finding: The company's own prospectus shows backlog of $1,111M at 2026-06-30, up from $419M at 2025-12-31, with book-to-bill of 3.5x for Q2 and 2.5x for H1. That covers the ~$464M H2 revenue implied by FY26 consensus of $901.7M about 2.4 times, which makes a Q3 revenue shortfall from lack of work unlikely. The cap: the Q3 bar is unsourced, and the tight consensus range ($898-904M) suggests the models are anchored to management's roadshow framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for ACCV (first print). The rule 'a prospectus backlog implying bookings far above what previews anchor on' has paid in this repo's resolved days (LESSONS.md, What has worked), but here the consensus already sits near the backlog-implied run rate.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. The backlog is public, but the stock trades at about $2.9B total equity value (225M shares x $12.8) against about $4.0B at an IPO that was itself priced below range. A market that believed the backlog converts on schedule, with the Q3 book-to-bill still above 1, would not have sold the stock 29% below the IPO price on political risk alone. What the print adds is the Q3 book-to-bill and the end-September backlog, which no aggregator carries.
findings.independence: Same company document as the gross-margin finding (the 424B4), but a different line (backlog and bookings rather than margin). The peer orders in finding 1 point the same way; that is a different source.

findings.finding: The prospectus shows gross margin compressing: about 26.6% for H1 2026 against 30.4% for H1 2025 and 32.3% for FY2025 (computed from the S-1 summary table). A post-IPO note attributes this to higher labor costs and project inefficiencies, and the S-1 risk factors name field rework, commissioning delays and change-order risk. If Q3 margin stays in the mid-20s while revenue beats, the quality of the beat is poor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No ACCV history. Peers set the comparison: Eaton's Electrical Americas margin was 29.8% (+230bp sequentially) and Vertiv's adjusted operating margin 25.2% (+290bp), so the sector is expanding margin while ACCV's was contracting.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, which is why the size is small. The compression is in the prospectus and in tickeron's 10-20 note. The FY26 EPS consensus of $0.50 on about $900M of revenue already embeds thin margins. If the market expected the compression to reverse, the stock would not trade 29% below the IPO price, and if it expected it to worsen, the 8 analysts would not all have Buy or Hold ratings.
findings.independence: https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-accelevation-holdings-accv-stock-down-4-00-today-19916/ (2026-10-20) cites margin pressure from labor costs and project inefficiencies. That is a secondary read of the same S-1, so it is partly the same document.

findings.finding: On its 10-28 call Microsoft cut its calendar-2026 capex outlook to about $170B from about $175B, citing delayed third-party data-center capacity deliveries; IREN's Childress, Texas campus is reported as one of the late providers. ACCV's revenue includes installation, and two hyperscale/colo customers were 61.2% of 2025 direct revenue, so commissioning slips at third-party sites are a revenue-timing risk for Q3 and for the Q4 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a sector read. It is a proxy: ACCV's customers are not named, and nothing confirms Microsoft or IREN as a counterparty. It stays unpriced only to the extent the call reveals that a top-two customer slipped its schedules.
findings.independence: https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/microsoft-msft-cfo-says-capital-expenditures-were-lower-than-guidance-in-q1-as-some-third-party-capacity-deliveries-we-expected-in-q1-were-delayed (CFO quote). It has no link to ACCV's own documents; the 61.2% concentration comes from the 424B4.

findings.finding: The stock ran about 28% into the print, from a $9.95 close on 11-05 to about $12.78 intraday on 11-12, including +11.5% on 11-11 and +7.3% on 11-12, with no company news (the last release was the 11-05 date notice). Part of a relief print is therefore already in the price. The 11-04/05 selloff itself was sector-wide: the Texas governor-elect's moratorium pledge, with Texas about 30% of projects, plus Democratic control of Congress. On the call management will have to answer on Texas exposure, which can cut either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for ACCV on earnings. In the past six weeks of sector shocks the stock has moved 1.3-2x Vertiv on the same days (-17.1% on 11-04 against Vertiv -12.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: This finding is itself a reading of what is priced. A 28% bounce in five sessions on no news means the market has already re-rated the political shock back toward a 'demand is intact' print, so a merely in-line quarter has less room to lift the stock.

findings.finding: Short interest is about 3.9M shares, up 38%, with 3.0 days to cover. Against the roughly 33M Class A shares not held by Olympus (120.0M Class A outstanding less 87.2M held directly by Accelevation Pubco Holdings LP per the 11-10 13G), that is about 12% of the true tradable float. A good print meets a meaningful short base in a thinly floated stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for ACCV. In this repo, shorts placed into names with 18% and 23% of float short squeezed for more than 20% (LESSONS.md section 7).
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators report the short as 3.3% (StockTitan) or 1.3% (MarketBeat) of float because they divide by the full Class A count. Divided by the float that actually trades it is about 12%, which few screens show. If the crowding were recognised the borrow fee would be rising; it fell to 4.1% by 10-25, though that reading predates the short build-up.
findings.independence: Short count from https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/ACCV/ (2026-11-12); borrow from https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/accv/borrow-fee/ (2026-10-25). The float denominator comes from the 13G.

findings.finding: On 10-09 ACCV refinanced its January 2025 MidCap Financial credit agreement with a Bank of America-led $250M Term Loan A and $400M revolver: SOFR+2.25%, maturity 2031, $150M drawn, leverage covenant 4.0x from Q1 2027. What the money buys is a lower-cost bank facility plus revolver capacity for working capital against a $1.1B backlog. That is a ramp, not distress, and lower interest expense helps the Q4 and FY27 EPS framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 2.55% on the 10-13 announcement (StockTitan), on a day of sector weakness.
findings.why_not_priced: The interest saving is an inference: the 8-K does not state the old facility's margin, and a MidCap private-credit facility is typically priced well above SOFR+2.25%. The Q3 P&L will show the first partial-quarter effect, and the FY guide will show the run-rate. If the saving were in the models, the FY26 EPS range ($0.42-0.56) would already sit higher relative to net income.
findings.independence: None beyond the same 8-K; the size is small for that reason.

outside_window.finding: The 180-day IPO lock-up (directed-share program and the general underwriter lock-up) runs to about late March 2027. Olympus controls 85.4% and holds 105M Class B plus 87.2M Class A, so the supply overhang is real, but it is dated far after this window.

Texas data-center permitting and grid audit: the 90th Legislature convenes in January 2027, when the PUCT is expected to seek expanded statutory authority, and the governor-elect's moratorium pledge cannot act before inauguration.

baseline_tension: No skew to read. The positive peer and backlog evidence cuts against the 29% drawdown from the IPO price but agrees with the 28% five-day bounce into the print, so part of a good print is already in the price. That is why p_up is held at 53 despite peers that beat and raised.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced): the Q3 bar has one source that conflicts with the FY-implied split, so the backlog-vs-consensus finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.7 and the peer finding trimmed from +1.5 to +1.2; p_up held at 53.
Rule 5 (proxy): the Microsoft capex-delay finding is macro-to-company with no confirmed counterparty, cut from -0.8 to -0.5 and kept filed.
Rule 7 (crowded short before a negative): about 12% of the true float is short, so the run-up/positioning negative was shrunk from -1.0 to -0.8.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the refinancing funds working capital against a $1.1B backlog, so it stays a small positive (+0.3), unchanged.
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 13 to 14 for a first public print with no history and 7-17% daily moves on sector news.
